name: Obed
overview: Obed is a male descendant of the tribe of Judah, known primarily as the son of Ruth and the father of Jesse. His lineage places him within the Messianic line, highlighting his role in God's providential plan as recorded in the book of Ruth. There are no additional notes provided about his life beyond these family connections.
namesAndTitles: The name Obed means 'servant' or 'worshiper,' reflecting a humble and devoted character. This proper name, not given directly by God, is recorded in Ruth 4:17 and aligns with the biblical theme of faithful service to the Lord.
familyAndRelationships: Obed is explicitly identified as the son of Ruth and, by inference, the son of Boaz. He is also explicitly noted as the father of Jesse, establishing his place in the genealogical line that leads to King David. Scripture does not record other family relationships beyond these.
scriptureSignificance: Obed holds a significant place in Scripture as the link between Ruth and Jesse, thereby connecting the Moabite Ruth to the Davidic lineage. His birth represents God's faithfulness in preserving His covenant promises through faithful individuals. Obed's role underscores the providential unfolding of salvation history, culminating in the coming of the Messiah.
